one_liner: BigCommerce offers a broad REST and GraphQL API. Free sandbox stores and self-serve API accounts give working credentials, and the vendor has an official storefront MCP server.
auth_notes: Store-level API accounts give a static access token sent as X-Auth-Token. App-level OAuth (authorization code) is used for apps registered in the Developer Portal, and a draft app can be installed on any store you own. Account-level tokens also exist.
access_notes: The free developer sandbox, or a free trial store, gives API credentials via Settings > API Accounts. Draft apps can be registered in the Developer Portal. A partnership is only needed to publish to the marketplace.
blocker_notes: Marketplace publishing needs a partnership, but that is not required to build and test a toolkit.

evidence.quote: The developer sandbox is free of charge.
Navigate to **Settings > API Accounts** in your store control panel. Create credentials with the scopes you need.
BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.
Store-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) include a static access token that does not change.
A BigCommerce partnership](https://www.bigcommerce.com/partners/) (required to publish apps to the App Marketplace).
For everything else, use the [REST and GraphQL APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference).
The BigCommerce MCP server lets AI agents interact with a BigCommerce storefront using purpose-built commerce tools.
